148.question: The sociological analysis of health focuses on...

options.A: the biochemical mechanisms of disease, laboratory diagnostics and pharmacology
options.B: the technique of surgical operations, the choice of drugs and methods of rehabilitation
options.C: statistics of marriages, divorces and births in families of different regions of the country
options.D: the patient's personal experiences, dreams, moods and inner motives
options.E: the links between health and living conditions, social relations and institutions

options.A: the effectiveness of surgical methods of treatment in different clinics of the country
options.B: the causes and spread of diseases in different social groups of the population
options.C: the biological mechanisms of hereditary diseases in individual people
options.D: the cost of medicines and the development of pharmaceutical markets worldwide
options.E: the psychological characteristics of doctors and their attitude to patients

150.question: The social determinants of health include...

options.A: working, living and educational conditions, and access to public resources
options.B: blood type, heredity, sex, age and a person's build
options.C: hemoglobin level, blood pressure, pulse, body temperature and weight
options.D: type of nervous system, temperament, and acuity of vision and hearing
options.E: the chemical composition of drugs, dosages, forms of release and shelf life

options.A: a person's voluntary refusal of treatment out of disbelief in the power of doctors and medicines
options.B: a person's legal release from work because of a sick leave certificate issued to them
options.C: the social devaluation of a person because of a condition or diagnosis attributed to them
options.D: the scientific classification of human diseases by their causes, symptoms and course
options.E: heightened attention from society to a person because of their merits, titles and awards

152.question: The concept of the sick role is associated with the name of...

options.A: the cost of medicines, the number of hospitals and the size of medical staff
options.B: perceived well-being and the capacity for everyday functioning
options.C: only the absence of diagnoses and the results of a patient's laboratory tests
options.D: the revenues of pharmaceutical companies, sales volumes and export quotas
options.E: biological age, heredity, height and body weight

154.question: The accessibility of medical care is characterized by...

options.A: the high qualifications of doctors and modern equipment in the leading clinics of the capital
options.B: the level of patient satisfaction with the doctor's work and the politeness of staff in the outpatient clinic
options.C: the share of state spending on health care in the country's gross domestic product
options.D: the life expectancy of the population and the death rate from heart disease in the country
options.E: the possibility of obtaining the necessary care given financial, territorial and organizational conditions

155.question: Unmet need for medical care means a situation in which a person...

options.A: needs care but does not receive it
options.B: receives care although they do not need it
options.C: seeks care and receives it immediately
options.D: is healthy and has regular check-ups
